# NPM Improved v1.2.2

NPM Improved v1.2.2 focuses on making the Control Center easier to move around and easier to understand.

## Better Settings navigation

Settings sections now have stable deep links using the `?section=` query parameter.

That means:

- refreshing a Settings page keeps you on the same section;
- browser back/forward navigation works between Settings sections;
- links can open Database, Instance Synchronization, Update, or another section directly;
- update alerts and Dashboard actions can take you straight to the relevant workspace.

Desktop Settings navigation now includes icons, short descriptions, a clearer selected state, and an update-available badge.

On smaller screens, the large Settings sidebar is replaced by a compact section selector.

## Better navigation from elsewhere in the Control Center

The footer update alert now opens **Settings → Update** instead of sending the administrator to GitHub.

The Dashboard high-availability action now opens **Settings → Instance Synchronization** directly.

The application header subtitle also follows the active Settings section so the current context remains obvious.

## Clearer Default Site workflow

Each Default Site mode now explains what it actually does:

- NPM Improved default page;
- HTTP 404;
- Nginx 444 connection close;
- redirect;
- custom HTML.

Template variables are displayed as easy-to-scan cards. Selecting a variable copies it and briefly confirms the copy action.

The underlying template behavior is unchanged: NPMX synchronizes the template, while each node renders its own local values.

## Better updater presentation

Release notes in **Settings → Update** now render as formatted Markdown rather than raw Markdown text.

Update state changes are also exposed through an ARIA live region so assistive technology can announce lifecycle progress.

## Certificate Lifecycle clarity

Certificate Lifecycle now has a clear section heading and short explanation before its controls.

## Updating

Existing supported installations can install v1.2.2 from **Settings → Update**.

The updater continues to use the normal GHCR image first and can fall back to the SHA-256-verified public GitHub Release image bundle when required.
